ambiguities.text: The specification does not detail what happens if the recipient address is a contract with no code
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the balance is unconditionally added regardless of whether the address is an EOA or contract, consistent with the 'MUST not fail' requirement.

ambiguities.text: The serialization 'RLP([transactions, [], withdrawals])' includes an empty list but its purpose is unclear
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the empty list is a placeholder for future use or backwards compatibility, not affecting current processing.

implicit_assumptions.description: Consensus layer validation of withdrawals is assumed to be correct and complete before passing to execution layer
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Invalid withdrawals could credit arbitrary amounts to arbitrary addresses if consensus validation is bypassed.

implicit_assumptions.description: The withdrawal index counter is maintained correctly across beacon chain and never resets or duplicates
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Duplicate withdrawal indices could allow replay attacks or double-crediting of withdrawal amounts.

implicit_assumptions.description: Engine API correctly transmits withdrawal data between consensus and execution clients
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Mismatched withdrawal data between layers could cause consensus failures or incorrect balance updates.

implicit_assumptions.description: The bounded quantity of withdrawals per block is sufficient to process validator exits in reasonable time
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Withdrawal queue could grow unboundedly if exit rate exceeds processing capacity.
